title: Which marked points sit on one segment, and which on two?
description: A zigzag path joins five marked points one after another, and each straight piece between two neighbouring points is named by its end points. Counting the pieces at each marked point shows which points are on one segment and which are on two. A last check counts the pieces from the number of points.
teaching_notes: One idea: a straight piece between two marked points is a line segment, and a bend is shared by two segments. Watch for students who forget that the two end points of the path belong to only one segment each.

source: Name the line segments in Fig. 2.4. Which of the five marked points are on exactly one of the line segments? Which are on two of the line segments?
video_script.why: The child names each straight piece of a zigzag path as a line segment and sees that the bends are shared by two segments.
video_script.substitution: Walk along the path and stop at every marked point.
video_script.anchor: a zigzag path through the five marked points L, M, P, Q and R, made of straight pieces
video_script.payoff_line: L and R are on exactly one segment, and M, P and Q are on two segments

final_answer.value: Segments LM, MP, PQ, QR. L and R are on exactly one segment; M, P and Q are on two segments
final_answer.spoken: the segments are L M, M P, P Q and Q R. L and R are on exactly one segment, and M, P and Q are on two segments

never_show: which points are on one segment and which on two, before the answer beat
maths_rules: The path goes through the marked points in the order L, M, P, Q, R, and each piece between neighbouring points is straight.
The five points in a row make four pieces: LM, MP, PQ and QR.
L is only on LM and R is only on QR, so each is on exactly one segment.
M is on LM and MP, P is on MP and PQ, Q is on PQ and QR, so each is on two segments.
Check: five points in a row make 5 - 1 = 4 pieces.
video_script.design: One idea: each straight piece is a line segment, and each bend belongs to two of them. The zigzag path stays on the board and the pieces light up one after another. The method is the same way as the example in the book on the line segment stretched into a line.
